rendered.overview: Five-color Aang Ally deck built around bending. [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] draws a card for every bend, and doing all four transforms him. Lessons, earthbenders and airbenders feed those triggers. A backup is an infinite loop using [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and an Aang that airbends.

strategy: Ramp with [[Bender's Waterskin]] and [[Hermitic Herbalist]], then cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Earthbend with [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] and [[Earthbending Lesson]] to draw cards off the commander.
Airbend with [[Airbending Lesson]] and [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], then firebend by attacking, to complete all four bends.
Transform into [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]]'s back face to draw four cards and deal 4 damage to each opponent.
Alternate win: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] with an airbending Aang and the commander loops for infinite triggers.

keep: [[Hermitic Herbalist]] with a bending spell sets up the commander.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] plus cheap Lessons starts earthbending.
sendBack: Hands missing a color source for most of the deck's spells.
Expensive Lessons with no early ramp to cast them.

cards: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
tips.text: [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbends on every spell, so each Lesson you cast also triggers [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] to draw.
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles Ally triggers such as [[Haru, Hidden Talent]] earthbending when an Ally enters.

rendered.overview: Jeskai artifact deck led by [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], a haste commander that proliferates whenever it taps. Mana rocks and cheap artifacts fill the board, proliferate pieces grow counters, and [[Lux Artillery]] or big attackers like [[Kappa Cannoneer]] close the game. Several listed combos give alternate wins.

strategy: Cast artifacts and mana rocks early, aiming to land [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3.
Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] or use [[Surge Conductor]] to proliferate and grow counters each turn.
Stack counters on creatures and artifacts with [[Steel Overseer]] and [[Contagion Engine]].
Finish with [[Lux Artillery]] at thirty counters or by attacking with [[Kappa Cannoneer]].
Backup: [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] makes infinite draw and loot triggers.

keep: [[Surge Conductor]] plus a cheap rock sets up proliferate early.
[[Everflowing Chalice]] with an artifact to follow.
sendBack: Only expensive proliferate pieces and no early artifacts.
Hands missing blue or white sources for the artifact spells.

tips.text: [[Surge Conductor]] proliferates each time another nontoken artifact enters, so [[Whir of Invention]] adds a trigger on top of fetching the artifact.
[[Steel Overseer]] adds counters to artifact creatures, including [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and each proliferate then adds another.
[[Deepglow Skate]] doubles counters on [[Lux Artillery]]-boosted creatures and artifacts, pushing toward the thirty counters needed.

weaknesses: Critical: Nearly every threat is an artifact, so [[Vandalblast]] or [[Collector Ouphe]] shuts down the deck.
Moderate: Only 6 interaction cards, so a fast combo or big threat can slip by; [[Swords to Plowshares]] handles just one creature.
Minor: Without [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] the deck still proliferates through other pieces but loses its main steady trigger.

plans.primary: Build a pile of artifacts and counters, then use [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and other proliferate effects to grow counters on creatures and artifacts until a counter payoff ends the game.
backups: Assemble [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] or [[Freed from the Real]] for infinite draw and loot triggers, or use [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite extra turns.

rendered.overview: A Colorless artifact-and-Eldrazi ramp deck led by [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]]. Rocks and utility lands push out big colorless spells that cascade twice, and annihilator bodies like [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]] close the game. [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] is an alternate route to infinite mana.

strategy: Play rocks like [[Thran Dynamo]] and [[Worn Powerstone]] to reach the commander's six mana early.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5, then follow with colorless spells of mana value 7 or more to cascade twice.
Land [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]] to make opponents sacrifice permanents each attack.
Backup: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] make infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Thran Dynamo]] or [[Worn Powerstone]] with a cheap play behind it.
sendBack: Hands of expensive Eldrazi with no rock to cast them.

tips.text: [[Basalt Monolith]] untaps for three mana, and [[Forsaken Monument]] adds an extra colorless per tap, so the pair makes infinite mana.
[[Eye of Ugin]] cuts colorless Eldrazi costs and can tutor a colorless creature such as [[Artisan of Kozilek]].

Minor: Wins lean on combat and annihilator, so [[Ghostly Prison]] slows the attacks.

rendered.overview: A Naya Dinosaur deck led by [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]]. Cost reducers and ramp put big Dinosaurs out early, enrage creatures turn damage into value, and trample attackers push damage through. [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] then reveals cards to drop more Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.

strategy: Cast cheap mana creatures and cost reducers like [[Kinjalli's Caller]] and [[Knight of the Stampede]] early.
Land big Dinosaurs such as [[Annoyed Altisaur]] and [[Pantlaza, Sun-Favored]] to chain free spells.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and trample creatures so combat damage reveals more Dinosaurs.
Use enrage creatures like [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to turn fights and damage into tokens and counters.
Backup: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] makes infinite tokens and damage.

keep: [[Kinjalli's Caller]] or [[Knight of the Stampede]] with ramp to cast Dinosaurs.
[[Pantlaza, Sun-Favored]] with the mana to cast it early.
sendBack: Expensive Dinosaurs with no ramp or cost reducers.
Only off-color spells with nothing green to cast.

tips.text: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] pings each creature when a Dinosaur enters, which triggers [[Polyraptor]] to copy itself each time.
[[Marauding Raptor]] deals 2 damage to each creature entering, so [[Ripjaw Raptor]] draws a card as it enters.
[[Rite of Passage]] adds a counter whenever [[Apex Altisaur]] survives damage, and it fights again on each hit.

Makes Dinosaur spells cost less.

Cascades into a free spell.

Copies itself when damaged.

Casts creatures from the top, makes Beasts.

weaknesses: Moderate: None of the 7 interaction cards is instant speed, so a fast combo from [[Thassa's Oracle]] cannot be stopped in time.
Moderate: Wins mostly through creature combat, so [[Propaganda]] or a fog slows the whole plan.
Minor: Three colors with many tapped lands and an 8-mana commander can stumble, and [[Blood Moon]] punishes the nonbasics.

plans.primary: Cheat Dinosaurs into play with cost reducers, ramp and cascade, then connect with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and other trampling Dinosaurs to flood the board.

Pair [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] with [[Walking Ballista]] to put infinite +1/+1 counters on the rest of the team.

rendered.overview: Mono-red Goblin tribal built around [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], which doubles the Goblin count each turn. Token makers and haste enablers like [[Goblin Chieftain]] turn the swarm into lethal attacks, while burn and sacrifice outlets finish the job. [[Skirk Prospector]] can also loop the commander with a lord.

strategy: Cast cheap Goblins like [[Mogg War Marshal]] and [[Dragon Fodder]] early to build a board for the commander.
Land [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4, then tap it each turn to double your Goblin count.
Give the swarm haste with [[Goblin Chieftain]] and [[Goro-Goro, Disciple of Ryusei]], then attack wide.
Convert Goblins into damage with [[Goblin Bombardment]], [[Pashalik Mons]] and [[Fireball]] to close out.
Backup win: [[Skirk Prospector]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and a lord like [[Goblin Warchief]] loop commander casts.

keep: [[Mogg War Marshal]] or [[Dragon Fodder]] with red mana to build a board.
sendBack: Expensive burn with no cheap Goblins to feed the commander.

tips.text: [[Goblin Bombardment]] turns each [[Mogg War Marshal]] token and its death trigger into extra damage, since it makes another Goblin when it dies.
[[Goblin Chieftain]] gives [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] tokens haste, so the new Goblins can attack the turn they are made.
[[Pashalik Mons]] pings whenever a Goblin dies, so sacrificing to [[Goblin Sledder]] adds damage.

keyCards.job: Doubles your Goblins each turn.
Gives Goblins haste and +1/+1.
Cheap bodies that feed Krenko's count.
Fetches a Goblin like Chieftain.
Pings on Goblin deaths, makes more Goblins.
Sacrifice outlet that starts the loop.
Cheaper Goblins and haste for the loop.
Turns Goblins into reach damage.

weaknesses: Moderate: Repeated removal like [[Swords to Plowshares]] on [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] slows the doubling and leaves a plain Goblin deck.
Moderate: Most wins come from a Goblin swarm, so [[Settle the Wreckage]] or a sweeper like [[Wrath of God]] can undo the board.
Minor: The deck cannot remove an opposing enchantment such as [[Rest in Peace]] or [[Propaganda]].

plans.primary: Build a growing army of Goblins with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and the cheap token makers, then swarm opponents with hasty Goblins and burn.
backups: Assemble [[Skirk Prospector]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and either [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] for infinite commander casts, hasty Goblin tokens and death triggers.
Finish with direct damage from [[Fireball]], [[Goblin Bombardment]] and [[Goblin Grenade]] by sacrificing Goblins.

rendered.overview: This Jeskai deck plays two partner commanders, [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]], alongside many God creatures. Experience counters feed +1/+1 counters each end step, proliferate effects stack them, and [[All Will Be One]] turns counters into damage. Extra combats finish games.

strategy: Cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] around turn 4 and attack with Gods to gain experience counters.
Each end step, [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] puts counters on a creature equal to your experience, and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] draws off those counters.
Proliferate with [[Flux Channeler]] and [[Inexorable Tide]] to grow counters further.
Alternate win: [[All Will Be One]] deals damage for every counter you add, ending the game without combat.
Backup: [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] give extra combats for a big attack.

keep: [[Flux Channeler]] or [[Inexorable Tide]] with early mana starts the counter plan.
A God like [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] with colored mana to cast it.
sendBack: Expensive enchantments with no early plays or ramp.
Hands missing white or red mana for the Gods.

tips.text: [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds an extra counter, so each [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] end step trigger puts one more counter on the creature.
[[All Will Be One]] with [[Inexorable Tide]] deals damage every time you cast a spell, since proliferate adds counters.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles proliferate, so [[Flux Channeler]] adds two counters per noncreature spell.

keyCards.job: Gains experience, adds counters each end step.
Converts experience into cards and damage.
Adds an extra counter to each placement.
Proliferates on noncreature spells.
Turns counters into damage to opponents.
God-less attacker that builds experience and tokens.
Grants extra combats for big attacks.

weaknesses: Moderate: Many enchantments and Gods are exposed to [[Vandalblast]] or [[Farewell]], which would stall counter and proliferate engines.
Moderate: Only 3 of 7 interaction cards are instant speed, so a fast combo from [[Thassa's Oracle]] may go unanswered.
Moderate: Combat-based wins are slowed by [[Propaganda]] or a fog effect.

Three colors with several tapped lands and painlands can stumble on early white or blue mana.

rendered.overview: Dimir Ninja aggro. Unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Tormented Soul]] connect, then ninjutsu swaps in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and other Ninjas for card advantage and life loss. Counterspells and cheap removal protect the attack, and extra-turn spells add more combat steps.

strategy: Cast cheap unblockable creatures such as [[Slither Blade]] and [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] early to start attacking.
Once a creature is unblocked, ninjutsu [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] in from the command zone around turn 3.
Each Ninja hit triggers [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] to draw and drain; [[Ingenious Infiltrator]] adds more cards.
Hold counterspells like [[Counterspell]] and [[Snuff Out]] to protect attackers and clear blockers.
Backup: chain extra turns with [[Temporal Manipulation]] and [[Time Warp]] for more attacks.

keep: [[Slither Blade]] plus a cheap Ninja starts the attack early.
[[Mistblade Shinobi]] with an unblockable attacker and blue mana.
sendBack: Expensive Ninjas with no cheap attacker to carry them.
Hands missing blue or black mana for ninjutsu.

tips.text: [[Satoru Umezawa]] gives creature cards in hand ninjutsu, so [[Dimir Infiltrator]] can swap in too, and each activation digs for more cards.
[[Silver-Fur Master]] cuts ninjutsu costs by one and pumps Ninjas, helping [[Fallen Shinobi]] come down cheaper.
[[Higure, the Still Wind]] can make a Ninja unblockable for {2}, and its hit searches up another Ninja like [[Throat Slitter]].

keyCards.job: Gives every creature in hand ninjutsu.
Cheaper ninjutsu and bigger Ninjas.
Draws on every Ninja hit.
Finds a Ninja and grants evasion.
Cheap unblockable attacker to enable ninjutsu.
Extra turn for another attack.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck wins almost only through combat damage, so a [[Settle the Wreckage]] or a [[Propaganda]] stalls it.
Minor: Ninjutsu costs need both blue and black, and painful lands like [[City of Brass]] add up.

plans.primary: Attack with cheap unblockable creatures, then ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and other Ninjas to draw cards and drain opponents off each hit.
backups: Take extra turns with [[Temporal Manipulation]], [[Temporal Trespass]] and [[Time Warp]] to get more Ninja attacks.
